question: A 2-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with a 3-minute episode of a tonic-clonic seizure. The parents deny any previous history of seizure involving the patient or the family. Physical examination reveals an afebrile, well-groomed, and playful appearance, with normal vital signs. The patient carries a pink birthmark on the right side of her face extending from the forehead to the zygomatic arch. Which of the following findings is most likely on a head CT of this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "2-year-old girl with tonic-clonic seizure" -> "possible underlying neurological condition" -> "pink birthmark on the face suggests Sturge-Weber syndrome" -> "Sturge-Weber syndrome associated with cortical malformations" -> "head CT likely shows calcifications" -> "prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Tonic-clonic seizure in a well child" -> "consider structural causes" -> "pink birthmark indicates possible vascular malformation" -> "Sturge-Weber syndrome is a possibility" -> "head CT may reveal associated findings" -> "prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Seizure without fever" -> "rule out metabolic or structural causes" -> "facial birthmark suggests Sturge-Weber syndrome" -> "Sturge-Weber syndrome can lead to calcifications" -> "head CT likely shows calcifications in the affected hemisphere" -> "prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Child with seizure and facial birthmark" -> "consider neurocutaneous syndromes" -> "Sturge-Weber syndrome is a candidate" -> "associated with cortical dysplasia and calcifications" -> "head CT findings consistent with this syndrome" -> "prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The 2-year-old girl with a tonic-clonic seizure and a facial pink birthmark is suggestive of Sturge-Weber syndrome, a neurocutaneous disorder characterized by facial capillary malformations and associated neurological complications. The presence of a facial birthmark, particularly a port-wine stain, raises the suspicion for this condition, which is known to cause cortical dysplasia and calcifications in the affected hemisphere. Consensus indicates that head CT findings in Sturge-Weber syndrome typically reveal prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcifications due to the underlying vascular malformations. Therefore, the most likely finding on a head CT for this patient is 'prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification.'
analysis: The clinical presentation of the 2-year-old girl, including the tonic-clonic seizure and the facial pink birthmark, is highly suggestive of Sturge-Weber syndrome. This condition is characterized by a facial capillary malformation (port-wine stain) and neurological manifestations, including seizures. The underlying pathology involves vascular malformations leading to cortical dysplasia and calcifications in the affected hemisphere. On head CT, the most characteristic finding associated with Sturge-Weber syndrome is prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcifications, which occur due to the abnormal vascular development. Given the information provided and the consensus in the medical literature regarding the expected findings in this syndrome, the most likely finding on a head CT for this patient is prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification.
